# FDG9022

> DO accept a `CancellationToken` parameter, named “cancellation-Token,” in asynchronous methods.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.2.2 Task-Based Async Pattern.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9022
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Accept a CancellationToken parameter named 'cancellationToken' in the asynchronous method '{0}'

FDG9022 reports an externally visible method that returns a task-like type (as for FDG9020) and has no CancellationToken parameter, or none named "cancellationToken" (the text breaks the name with a hyphen at a line end; every example writes cancellationToken). A missing parameter is not reported when another overload with the same name in the type accepts a CancellationToken, as Stream.ReadAsync does in the FDG9032 body, or on DisposeAsyncCore, which the Dispose Pattern declares without one (FDG9082), or on a static method that only returns completed tasks, which FDG9020 leaves out for the same reason (it starts no operation to cancel). Overrides and interface implementations are not reported, and private and internal methods are not checked, so coverage is partial. Several examples in the chapter leave the parameter out to show other rules (FDG9019, FDG9029, FDG9043, FDG9044); they are reported. Adding or renaming a parameter changes the public signature, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

Long-running operations generally warrant an “abort” option, and asynchronous operations tend to be long-running. The Task-Based Async Pattern uses the `System.Threading.CancellationToken` type to control cancelations.

```csharp
// Incorrect: The caller has no way of cancelling this operation
public Task WriteAsync(string text) { ... }

// Correct: Cancellation is supported, as an optional parameter
public Task WriteAync(
  string text,
  CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) { ... }
```
